synthesis: Scout users who forget their email or password have no recovery mechanism, creating permanent lockout without admin assistance. Current onboarding sends a one-time signed URL for password setup that cannot be reused after email_verified_at is set. The ticket proposes two solutions: (1) admin password reset OR (2) magic-link/passwordless like Clarity (PREFERRED). Clarity admin panel already implements a working OTP (One Time Password) passwordless system via OneTimePassword class and CustomLoginPage that can be adapted for Scout. Scout currently uses traditional email+password login via ClarityScoutAuthController::login returning Sanctum tokens. Admin actions in ScoutUsersResource include force-login (impersonation) and resend-onboarding (only works pre-verification), but no password reset capability exists.
scope: Add OTP passwordless authentication to Scout login flow (preferred path)
Update ClarityScoutAuthController::login to accept OTP in addition to or instead of password
Update Login.vue to support email-only + OTP input pattern (mirror Clarity's CustomLoginPage UX)
Add admin action to ScoutUsersResource for triggering password/account recovery
Create recovery notification that sends OTP or signed recovery link
Handle case where user forgot email: admin must identify user, trigger recovery to known email
Ensure org-scoped security maintained (prior force-login org-scoping work precedent: Scout tokens must stay org-scoped)
Tests: OTP login path in ClarityScoutAuthControllerTest, admin action tests, integration test for recovery flow
Decision required: keep password auth as fallback or remove entirely (impacts existing users)
Decision required: migrate existing users (null out passwords?) or grandfather password auth

questions.q: Should password authentication be removed entirely or kept as fallback?
questions.notes: Removing simplifies security surface but breaks existing user habits. Keeping requires dual-path testing. Ticket says PREFERRED passwordless but doesn't mandate password removal

questions.q: How do we migrate existing Scout users with passwords set?
questions.notes: Options: (1) null out passwords and force OTP, (2) grandfather password auth for existing users, (3) prompt password users to switch to OTP on next login

questions.q: Should onboarding flow change to OTP-only (skip set-password step)?
questions.notes: If we go full passwordless, onboarding should skip password setup and just send OTP on first login. Simpler UX

questions.q: What happens if user has no access to their email at all?
questions.notes: Requires admin to update email address first. Should ScoutUsersResource allow email updates? Currently new_user_email and existing_user_email fields exist but behavior on post-verification edit unclear

questions.q: Should OTP be cached per-user or per-email like Clarity?
questions.notes: OneTimePassword::put uses 'otp_'.$user->email as cache key. This is fine for Scout since email is unique per org

questions.q: Do we need rate limiting on OTP send for Scout?
questions.notes: Clarity uses throttle on login form. Scout login already has throttle:5,1. May need separate throttle for OTP send action

Verify admin recovery action works for verified users (email_verified_at NOT NULL). Test org-scoping: user in org A cannot use recovery link meant for user in org B even with same email. Test forgot email scenario: admin must identify user by kit/name/phone, then send recovery. Test existing password users if keeping fallback: can still login with password, can also use OTP
escalate_reason: Auth changes = escalate bias per instructions. This modifies authentication flow (adding OTP, potentially removing password requirement), touches security-sensitive surfaces (login controller, token generation), and has org-scoping implications flagged by prior force-login org-scoping work precedent. While technically straightforward (reusing proven OTP infrastructure), auth changes require security review and explicit approval on password removal vs fallback decision
